paper.title: Automated Formal Proofs of Combinatorial Identities via Wilf-Zeilberger Guidance and LLMs

read: full text (arXiv HTML): Sections 1-6; appendices (glossary, RL set construction, data details) not read

claims.claim: Formal Lean 4 proofs of classical combinatorial identities can be found far more often by combining the Wilf-Zeilberger method, which reduces an identity to a recurrence lemma and boundary obligations, with a language-model prover specialised by training only on kernel-verified proofs, than by language-model provers alone. Supported only if, at 32 attempts per identity on 100 identities drawn from sources disjoint from training (with canonical forms checked against leakage), the combined system proves at least three times as many as the best open prover and more than a frontier general model; and if the specialised prover also proves more problems than the base prover on two broader combinatorics benchmarks.
claims.decision_rule: LCI-Test pass@32: WZ-LLM >= 3x best baseline prover (34 vs 9) and > Gemini-3.1-Pro (16); CombiBench and PutnamBench-Comb above Goedel-Prover-V2.

claims.claim: Splitting a proof into symbolic sub-goals helps a language-model prover only if the prover can discharge nearly all of them, because one unproved obligation leaves the whole proof incomplete. Supported only if giving the Wilf-Zeilberger decomposition to an untrained general prover adds no end-to-end proofs, with that prover proving under half of the sub-goal lemmas and completing none of the decomposed identities, whereas with the specialised prover lemma accuracy exceeds 70% and most decomposed identities are completed; and if on benchmarks where few problems fit the method the decomposition adds at most a few proofs.
claims.decision_rule: WZ-Sketch + Goedel = Goedel alone (9/100); Goedel lemma acc 47.88%, 0/46 completed; WZ-Prover 73.34%, 29/46; sketch route adds only 1 on CombiBench and PutnamBench-Comb.

experiments.text: Build the decomposition and the benchmark. Setup: normalise each Lean statement to a canonical summation form (shift ranges, rewrite bounded sums, split parity cases); for identities the Wilf-Zeilberger method covers, have SageMath synthesise the rational certificate and generate Lean obligations: the recurrence lemma, boundary terms, non-vanishing side conditions for denominators, normalisation lemmas and case branches; identities it does not cover become direct proving targets. Benchmark LCI-Test: 100 identities from two classical collections reserved for testing, with canonical forms checked to be absent from training. Success means the whole proof is accepted by the Lean 4 kernel within 32 attempts.

Train the specialised prover. Setup: start from Goedel-Prover-V2 (8B); fine-tune on 307 hand-formalised textbook identities with full proofs plus 1,200 extracted lemma proofs; run two rounds of expert-in-the-loop bootstrapping on 1,020 candidate identities, keeping only kernel-verified outputs (5,671 lemma proofs and 111 identity proofs added); then DAPO reinforcement learning with a verification reward and a soft length penalty on a difficulty-smoothed set (near-duplicate easy goals downsampled, near-zero-pass-rate goals removed). Training costs 16 GPU-days on 4 L40s.

Compare end-to-end proof success on LCI-Test. Result: DeepSeek-V3 1/100, InternLM-2.5-StepProver 2/100 (with a 4 x 32 x 600 search budget), MA-LoT 3/100, Kimina-Prover-Distill and DeepSeek-Prover-V2 6/100, Goedel-Prover-V2 9/100, Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview 16/100; the specialised prover alone 12/100; the full system 34/100, of which 29 come through the decomposition route and 5 are identities outside the method's coverage proved directly.

Test on broader combinatorics benchmarks. Setup: CombiBench (100 problems) and the 36 combinatorics-tagged problems of PutnamBench, pass@32. Result: CombiBench 6, 8 and 12 for Kimina, DeepSeek-Prover-V2 and Goedel-Prover-V2 against 15 for the specialised prover alone and 16 for the full system; PutnamBench-Comb 0, 2 and 0 against 3 and 3.

Separate the training stages. Setup: the prover after seed fine-tuning only, after expert iteration, and after DAPO, on LCI-Test without decomposition at pass@1, 8 and 32. Result: 1 / 3 / 9, then 3 / 6 / 10, then 4 / 6 / 12, with the reinforcement-learning gain concentrated at 32 attempts.

Give the decomposition to the untrained prover. Setup: the same Wilf-Zeilberger sub-goals discharged by Goedel-Prover-V2 instead of the specialised prover, pass@32. Result: 9/100 on LCI-Test, identical to Goedel-Prover-V2 without decomposition; 13/100 on CombiBench (one more) and 0/36 on PutnamBench-Comb (no change).

Diagnose at the level of lemmas. Setup: the 1,178 sub-goals produced for the 46 LCI-Test identities the method decomposes, attempted by each prover. Result: Goedel-Prover-V2 proves 564 (47.88%) and completes 0 of 46 identities; the specialised prover proves 864 (73.34%) and completes 29 of 46. On CombiBench and PutnamBench-Comb, where few problems are identities of this type, the decomposition route contributes only 1 proof each.

notes: The abstract mentions 5 identities a symbolic-only baseline fails on; the main text reports these as the 5 WZ-uncovered identities proved directly.
